title: AuraGen
desc: A biotech brand built to prove its own credibility

blocks.title: AuraGen
blocks.lede: A biotech company that doesn’t exist — built to test whether a brand can prove its own credibility.

items.label: Role
items.value: Concept, brand, product design, front-end build, AI direction

items.label: Scope
items.value: Identity, design system, interactive website, working dashboard prototype

items.statement: Most biotech websites ask you to believe them.
body: They say they are rigorous. Data-driven. Scientific. Investor-ready.
Then they show you a polished screenshot and ask you to take their word for it.
AuraGen started as a test of the opposite approach.
I invented the company so I could build the kind of investor site I wanted to see.
Instead of showing a static picture of the product, the site contains a working piece of it: an interactive lab dashboard with simulated operational data.

blocks.text: Don’t tell me it works — log me in.

body: The brand and design system were established first, by hand. AI entered later, at specific points where it could increase speed without making the creative decisions: scaling the system across the site and helping build the functioning experience.
That distinction matters to me. The experiment wasn’t “how much can AI do?” It was “how much can a designer direct when AI becomes part of the production pipeline?”
Identity, logotype, visual language, interface foundations, an investor-facing website and a live internal dashboard demonstration — all built as one connected system.

AuraGen sits somewhere between brand work, product design and creative technology. More than a fictional biotech company, it is a working test of how traditional design judgement and AI-assisted making can coexist without one quietly replacing the other.
